trust_decision.summary: Before redirecting the browser at the end of an external-IdP login, the server decides whether the caller-supplied redirectUri is one of the client application's registered redirect URIs by string comparison plus an opt-in prefix match, and delivers the one-time login code to the requested URI when that prefix match succeeds.

landing_point.why: The summary names the external auth callback; this is the only place where login.code is appended to a caller-supplied redirect URI (external.ts:142-143) after a partial/prefix match was allowed (external.ts:127).

fix_sites.entry_point: exported library API getClientRedirectUri(client, requestedUri, allowPartial) - also reached from GET/POST /oauth2/authorize (oauth/authorize.ts:77), POST /oauth2/register (oauth/register.ts:26) and getStandardClientByRedirectUri (oauth/clients.ts:42)
fix_sites.module_kind: library/utility (server oauth module, not the module the report names)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The shared matcher in oauth/clients.ts already defaults to exact matching and no other caller passes allowPartial=true, so an engineer can argue the oauth module needs no change and that the leak is confined to the /auth/external handler - which is exactly the site the published fix also hardened.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legacy clients registered as https://example.com/callback must keep working when the request appends query parameters (https://example.com/callback?param=value); pinned unit tests assert this partial match succeeds, and the published fix keeps it behind a project-level opt-in, so a fix that simply deletes partial matching breaks tested and deployed backwards compatibility.

O6_input_shapes: registered URI plus extra path segments (https://example.com/callback/extra)
look-alike/different host (registered URI string with a foreign host appended: .../auth/callback.evil.com)
deprecated scalar ClientApplication.redirectUri instead of the redirectUris array
unparseable URI (new URL throws; new predicate returns false)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Same callback's returnTo fallback picks the post-login redirect target with a pathname prefix match (returnToUrl.pathname.startsWith(allowed.pathname)) instead of an exact/segment match, and the redirect carries the Login id which GET /auth/login/:login (unauthenticated) turns into the login code.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: returnTo is not the OAuth redirect_uri, its redirect carries login/scope/nonce but not the code, protocol/host/port are compared exactly, and the list is the operator's own DomainConfiguration.allowedPostLoginRedirectUrls - a plausible 'neighbouring feature, already allow-listed' dismissal.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and package as the landing point; ~130 lines below the fixed hunk

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SPA /oauth page hands the authorization code to params.get('redirect_uri') taken verbatim from the page URL, with no lookup of the client application's registered redirect URIs (second implementation of the same code-delivery step, in another package).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Client-side page in a different package, normally reached only through the server's authorize redirect which already performed the exact check (oauth/authorize.ts:299-305), so it can be argued to perform no authorization decision of its own.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 packages (packages/app, packages/react) away from packages/server/src/auth/external.ts; the page is fed by react/src/auth/SignInForm.tsx:114-121

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a partial/prefix fallback when resolving a standard client by redirect_uri during dynamic client registration
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file already imports the same matcher (oauth/register.ts:4) and RFC 7591 clients often register a URI that differs by a trailing path segment; a maintainer adding a 'legacy clients' fallback here would repeat exactly the mistake the published fix removes.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second redirect decision (returnTo) inside the same handler, reusing the prefix-matching style
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already has two redirect paths, so a reviewer adding a landing-page redirect naturally copies the neighbouring prefix logic instead of writing an exact matcher.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: redirect_uri re-verification at the authorization_code token exchange using the same matcher with allowPartial
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleAuthorizationCode does not check redirect_uri at all today, so a maintainer hardening code exchange would reach for getClientRedirectUri and could enable the legacy partial flag 'for backwards compatibility'.

O9_family: Improper redirect-URI validation leading to authorization-code leakage / open redirect (insufficient verification of data authenticity), OAuth redirect_uri prefix matching

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces monorepo; packages/server builds with tsc + build.mjs and tests with jest (babel-jest) via `npm test` in packages/server
O10_build.project_tests: packages/server/src/auth/external.test.ts (mocks node-fetch for the IdP token call), packages/server/src/oauth/clients.test.ts, packages/server/src/oauth/authorize.test.ts, packages/server/src/oauth/register.test.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the partial call in external.ts:127 with an exact-only check (drop the allowPartial argument), leaving the startsWith partial matcher in oauth/clients.ts:69 and the legacy-client compatibility path untouched.
